Before leaving, run a wash to clear any dirty dishes. When it finishes, unload the dishwasher, let the interior cool, clean the filter according to the user manual, and wipe the door seals with a soft, damp cloth. [P1]

For an extended absence, switch off the electricity supply and close the dishwasher’s water supply valve. Leave the door slightly open if it’s safe to do so, to help moisture escape. If the cottage could freeze, ask a qualified installer about draining the appliance. [P1]

When you return, restore both supplies and check for leaks before running a wash. [P1]

For an Ashby tumble dryer, leave guests these instructions: clean the lint filter after every load; check care labels and don’t tumble-dry unsuitable items; avoid overloading the drum and keep the area around it clear. Ask guests to stay in the property while it runs and let the programme finish, including its cooling stage. [P1]

For a Keel washing machine, ask guests to check the inlet and drain hoses for leaks or damage, turn on the water supply before washing, choose a programme suited to the care labels, and measure detergent for the load and local water hardness. [P2]

The passages conflict: one states a two-year warranty from purchase [P1], while another says 66 months from delivery [P2]. Check your warranty documents or contact Halvard Home to confirm which applies.

Stop cooking and switch off the hob using its controls. Check that the control area is clean and dry, and let hot surfaces cool before wiping them. [P2] If it’s safe to access the wall isolator, you can switch it off for 60 seconds and restore power. [P2]

If the error returns, leave the hob switched off and contact Halvard Home support. Note exactly what the display shows and when it happens. Don’t remove the glass or attempt internal repairs. [P2]

Stop the programme, switch off and unplug the dryer, and let it cool. Clean and refit the fluff filter; if it has a water tank, empty and refit it. Check that clothing isn’t caught in the door, then close it firmly. Reconnect the dryer and try the programme again. [P1]

If the error is a displayed fault code, note it, unplug the dryer for five minutes, then—while it is cool and unplugged—clear lint from the filter and check accessible air vents. Empty and refit the water container if present, then try starting a programme once. If the warning or code returns, stop using the dryer and contact Halvard Home support with the light or code and your model details. Don’t remove panels or attempt internal repairs. [P2]

Frost or ice inside the dishwasher is not normal. Don’t start a programme; switch the dishwasher off and contact Halvard Home support for advice before using it again. Don’t use boiling water or a sharp tool to remove the ice. [P1]

Stop the dryer immediately, switch it off and unplug it if it’s safe to do so. Don’t run another cycle to test it. [P1] Leave it unplugged until it has cooled completely; if there’s no sign of fire, you can then clear fluff from the lint filter and check that the external air vents are clear. [P1] Don’t use it again until a qualified appliance technician has checked it. [P1]

If there’s smoke or flame, keep the door closed, leave the property and call 999. Don’t use water or try to move the dryer. [P1]

Set a scheduled start for the time you want the heating to begin—not a delay duration. For example, if you want it to start one hour after 18:00, set the start time to 19:00, choose your target temperature, and save. Make sure the schedule is enabled and applies to the right day. [P1]

Switch off and unplug the dryer, pulling the plug rather than the lead, and let it cool completely. Remove the laundry, clean the lint filter, empty any water tank, and disconnect and secure any hoses or fittings. [P1][P2]

Plan a clear route, keep children and pets away, and use two people with suitable handling equipment, such as an appliance trolley. Keep the dryer upright; never lift it by the door, control panel, power lead, or fittings. Protect the cabinet and secure the dryer and loose connections for transport. [P1][P2]

At the new location, place it on a firm, level floor, reconnect it according to its installation instructions, and check that it is stable and undamaged. Keep it unplugged for 38 hours after moving before switching it on. [P1][P2]

Check that the extractor’s wall switch or fused spur is on, then try the light and fan controls to see whether the whole appliance has lost power or just the display. [P1]

Switch it off at the electrical supply for 60 seconds, turn it back on, and try the controls again. Keep your hands dry when operating switches. [P1]

If the fan and light work but the display stays blank, contact Halvard Home support and tell them which controls still respond. If nothing works, check whether other kitchen appliances have power; don’t remove covers or touch internal wiring, and arrange a qualified inspection if the problem continues. [P1]
Keep the extractor running for 10 minutes after cooking to clear lingering steam and smells. [P2]

If you mean a Keel washing machine, finish any wash programme, empty the drum, leave it switched on and connect it to your home Wi‑Fi. In the Halvard Home app, select the machine and go to **Settings > Firmware update**. Tap **Install** if an update is available, and wait for the app to confirm it’s complete before using the machine. [P1]

If you mean an Ashby tumble dryer, finish any drying programme, empty the drum, and leave it switched on and connected to Wi‑Fi. On the dryer’s display, open **Settings > Software update > Check for updates**, then select **Install** if an update is available. Wait for the display to confirm completion before using it. [P2]
Hire a qualified heat pump installer to disconnect, move and recommission your heating system. [P1]

To safely relocate your built-in Corra induction hob:

1. Switch it off and let the glass cool completely; remove cookware and loose items. [P1][P2]
2. Have a qualified electrician isolate and disconnect a hardwired hob. Do not cut, pull or lift it by its cable. [P1][P2]
3. Ask the installer to release any fixings or seals; do not force the hob out of the worktop. [P2][P1]
4. Use two people or suitable lifting equipment, supporting the appliance’s body—not the glass edges, controls or cable. Protect the glass and secure the hob against sliding or impact during transport. [P2][P1]
5. Do not tilt it more than 54 degrees while carrying it. [P1]
6. After moving it, wait 17 hours before switching it on, and have a qualified installer check and reinstall it before use. [P1][P2]

At the new location, ensure the installation is stable, properly ventilated, and electrically safe. If the hob was dropped, struck, exposed to water, or carried beyond the stated restriction, leave it disconnected and have it checked. [P1]
Yes. A factory reset of the Lumen smart thermostat clears saved Wi-Fi details, heating schedules, and personal settings, so you’ll need to set them up again afterward. [P1]

Send the service team the hob’s full model details and a clear photo of the part you want to replace, if you still have it. Include a short description of what you need—or describe the part’s purpose if it’s missing. [P1]

Make sure Mira is online in the Halvard Home app and that you can start a cleaning from the app. In your voice assistant’s app, open the section for adding smart home devices, search for and select Halvard Home, then sign in with the same Halvard Home account you used to set up Mira and allow access. Ask the assistant to discover devices, give the vacuum a simple name such as “Mira,” then try saying, “Start Mira.” [P1]

If Mira doesn’t appear, check its internet connection, unlink Halvard Home in the assistant’s app, and link it again. [P1]

Make sure the controller is powered on and your phone is connected to home Wi‑Fi. Turn on Bluetooth, keep the phone close to the controller, and allow the app any requested Bluetooth, nearby-device, or local-network permissions. Then fully close and reopen the app and try adding the controller again. [P1]

If it still doesn’t appear, restart your phone and check for app updates. Avoid factory-resetting the controller as an initial step; if the problem continues, contact the manufacturer’s support team and describe what you’ve tried. [P1]

The passages give conflicting durations: the Brio kettle warranty is described as 47 months from delivery [P1] and as two years from purchase [P2]. A separate guarantee for paid repairs lasts 122 days [P5]. I could not find a single, unambiguous guarantee period for your water boiler.

If you’re leaving food inside, keep the fridge freezer running, set the fridge to 4°C and the freezer to −18°C, and make sure both doors close properly. Remove food that will expire before you return. [P1]

If you’re emptying it for the long absence, switch it off and unplug it before cleaning. Remove all food, let any ice thaw, clean with warm water and mild detergent, and dry it thoroughly. Leave both doors ajar to help prevent smells and mould. [P1]

Cold weather can make the extractor’s surfaces cold, so warm, moist air from cooking condenses into water droplets. This is more likely in winter, especially if the extraction duct runs through an unheated space. [P1]

Switch the washer off at the socket and unplug it, then turn off the water and disconnect the inlet hose. Drain remaining water according to the user manual, empty and dry the drum, and keep a towel and shallow tray nearby for spills. [P1]

Refit the original transit bolts as directed in the manual to secure the drum. If they are missing, contact Halvard Home before moving the washer. Secure the hoses and cable so they cannot swing loose, become trapped or stretch during transport. [P1][P2]

Plan a clear route, keep the washer upright where possible, and use two people or suitable lifting equipment—do not carry it alone. [P1][P2]

For the Keel washer, note which warning light is flashing and wait for the drum to stop. Don’t force the door open; check that it’s firmly closed and no clothing is caught in the seal. [P2]

If the warning continues, switch off and unplug the washer for five minutes. With the power disconnected, check that the water tap is open and the inlet hose isn’t kinked. Reconnect it and try the programme again. [P2]

If the light keeps flashing, contact Halvard Home support and tell them which light is flashing and when it started. [P2]
Icy or damp buildup can happen when warm, moist air enters the refrigerator. Frequent door opening, uncovered food, or a poor door seal can make it worse. [P1]

Provide the full model details from the cooker hood’s rating label and the name or description of the accessory you need. If you’re unsure what it’s called, send a clear photo of the existing accessory. [P1] Before confirming the order, ask support to check compatibility and availability, and confirm the total price including delivery and the expected delivery time. [P1]

Switch on the child lock by pressing and holding the power button for 3 seconds while the Mira is switched on and stationary. A sound confirms the lock is active. It blocks the vacuum’s buttons, but scheduled cleaning and app controls remain available, so disable those too if you need to prevent automatic starts. [P1]

Keep your toddler away from the vacuum while it is moving, and don’t let children play with its controls. [P1][P2]

Place the Mira robot vacuum on its plugged-in charging dock. Press and hold the **Power** and **Home** buttons together for 10 seconds, then release them when you hear the reset announcement. Leave it on the dock while it restarts. Afterward, add it again in the Halvard Home app, reconnect it to Wi-Fi, and recreate any maps or cleaning schedules. The reset clears saved Wi-Fi details, schedules, and maps. [P1]

Have a qualified heat pump installer disconnect the unit and safely recover its refrigerant; don’t cut pipes, open the refrigerant circuit, or dismantle it yourself. [P1] Arrange recycling through your replacement installer or ask your local council for a service that accepts heat pumps, checking collection arrangements first. [P1] Keep the disconnected unit upright and away from children while awaiting collection, and use a licensed waste carrier if arranging transport yourself. [P1]
Check the power supply first: make sure the plug is fully inserted and the wall socket is switched on. [P1] You can test the socket with a lamp you know works. [P1]
Your Vale fridge freezer requires a 2.4 GHz Wi‑Fi network. [P1]

Try setting your heating to 19°C and lowering it by 1°C if everyone stays comfortable; use a schedule that fits your routine and a small overnight reduction rather than switching a heat pump off completely. [P1][P2] Keep hot-water hygiene settings unchanged. [P1]

You can also reduce electricity use by simmering food at a lower hob setting, using lids and only heating the water you need. [P4] Set your fridge to 4°C and freezer to −18°C, and keep their doors closed as much as possible. [P5]

Switch off the vacuum and remove it from the charging dock. Check for dust, hair or small objects around the opening, hinges and catch, and wipe accessible edges with a dry, soft cloth. Make sure the dust bin is seated correctly and nothing sticks out above it. Lower the cover gently; don’t force it shut. If it still won’t close or a hinge or catch looks damaged, stop using the vacuum and contact Halvard Home support. [P1]
First, check the hood’s power supply: make sure its wall switch or fused connection switch is on, and if it has a plug, check that it is fully inserted only if you can reach it safely. [P1]

Contact Halvard Home customer support with your washer’s model details and a description of the part you need. Explain that it’s an additional item, and ask them to confirm compatibility, availability, total price including delivery, and expected delivery time before ordering. [P1]

Unplug the teapot and let it cool completely, then empty it. Use a descaler labelled as suitable for kettles, following the package instructions; don’t overfill or mix cleaning products. Rinse thoroughly, then boil and discard a full kettle of fresh water twice before making drinks. Keep the base, plug, and outside dry, and never immerse the kettle in water. [P1]

Check that food or packaging isn’t blocking the door, push drawers fully in, and make sure shelves are seated correctly. Clean the door seal and the surface it touches with a soft cloth and warm water, then dry them. Look for ice preventing the door from closing, but don’t use sharp tools or force the door shut. [P1]

If it still hangs unevenly or the seal is split, contact Halvard Home support. [P1]

Switch it off and unplug it, then let it cool completely. Lift it off its base and wipe it dry; check whether water ran down from the spout or lid, and make sure it wasn’t filled above the MAX mark. If water keeps collecting underneath, stop using it and contact Halvard Home support. Don’t immerse the base or try to repair it yourself. [P1][P2]

First, check that the controller’s power supply is on. If there’s a clearly labelled wall switch, make sure it’s on; if it already is, switch it off for 30 seconds and turn it back on. Don’t remove the cover or touch wiring. [P1]

On your Tessa dishwasher, open **Settings** on the control panel, select **Firmware update**, then **Check for updates**. Make sure it’s connected to home Wi‑Fi, switched on, empty, and not running a wash programme. If an update is available, select **Install** and follow the display instructions. Keep the power and Wi‑Fi connected, and wait for the display to confirm it’s complete before starting a wash. [P1]

Pause the programme and wait for the drum to stop. If the door unlocks, spread heavy items evenly around the drum, then restart the programme; don’t force the door open. [P1]

Check that the machine is on a hard, level floor, all four feet touch the floor, and it doesn’t rock when gently pushed. If it was newly installed, check the installation guide to confirm the transit bolts were removed. [P1]

If strong vibration continues, stop using the machine and contact Halvard Home support. [P1]

Stop the cycle and turn off the water supply tap. If the plug and surrounding area are dry, switch off and unplug the machine; never touch a wet plug or socket. [P1]

Once it is safe, wipe up the water and, without moving the machine, check visible inlet-hose connections, whether the drain hose has slipped out, and whether water is running from the detergent drawer (too much detergent can cause excess foam and leaks). [P1]

Do not run another cycle while the leak is unexplained. If the hoses appear secure or the water is coming from beneath the casing, contact Halvard Home support. [P1]

Before first use:

- Read the supplied installation instructions and check the space and clearance requirements. [P1]
- Choose a dry, ventilated indoor location, away from water, heat sources and open flames; keep the required clearance and ventilation openings unobstructed. [P2]
- Place the dryer on a firm, level floor and adjust its feet so it stands steadily without rocking. [P1]
- Remove all packaging from inside and around the drum, and keep loose packaging away from children. [P1][P2]
- Connect any vent hose or drainage as directed in the supplied instructions. [P1][P2]
- Plug it directly into a suitable earthed wall socket—do not use an extension lead or adaptor—and make sure the plug remains accessible. [P1][P2]
- Wipe the empty drum with a soft, damp cloth. [P1]

Do not connect the dryer if its casing, plug or cable is damaged, or if you are unsure about the electrical supply; seek qualified help. [P1][P2]

Stop cleaning and switch off the vacuum. If the dock or plug is wet, switch off the mains socket before handling it. [P1]

Remove and empty the water tank over a sink, check that its filler cap is fully closed, and inspect the tank and outlet for cracks. Wipe the tank and vacuum underside dry; don’t rinse the vacuum body or return it to the dock while wet. [P1]

If the tank is cracked or it leaks again after you refit it securely, stop using the mopping function and contact Halvard Home support. [P1]

Make sure the heat pump is switched on and your phone is connected to your home Wi‑Fi. Then try, in order: move your phone closer to the heat pump; allow the app any requested Bluetooth or local network access; turn your phone’s Wi‑Fi off for 10 seconds and back on; fully close and reopen the app, then try adding the device again; and check for an app update. [P1]

If it still doesn’t appear, contact Halvard Home support and tell them your phone model and what happens when you try to connect. [P1]

Make sure the washing machine is switched on and your phone is nearby. Connect your phone to a **2.4 GHz Wi-Fi network**—5 GHz won’t work for setup—turn on Bluetooth, and allow the app to access nearby devices. Then close and reopen the app and try adding the machine again, following its pairing instructions. [P1]

If it still doesn’t appear, restart your phone and router, then try again once Wi-Fi is available. If the problem continues, contact Halvard Home support and tell them your phone model and where setup stops. [P1]

Yes. Water beneath the outdoor unit can be normal during or shortly after defrosting, when melted ice drains from the outdoor coil. [P1] Monitor it to see whether it stops; if water runs continuously, arrange an inspection by a qualified heat pump engineer. [P1]
Orrin heat pumps warm your home gradually, so the radiators may feel cooler than radiators connected to a boiler. This does not necessarily mean there is a fault. [P1]
The Fenwick cooker hood needs a 2.4 GHz home wi-fi network; it cannot connect to a network set to 5 GHz only. [P1]
No. The Halvard Home Brio kettle does not have a timer or delay-start setting; you must switch it on manually each time you want to boil water. [P1]
Yes. A gentle rumbling or hissing sound while your Brio kettle heats up is usually normal. [P1]

A new rattling, thumping or scraping noise may be caused by loose objects in the drum, metal zips or buttons, an uneven load, or the dryer touching nearby furniture. [P1]

Stop the programme, switch off and unplug the dryer before checking. Once the drum has cooled, remove the laundry and check for loose items; redistribute bulky items evenly, and make sure the dryer stands level and does not touch a wall or cupboard. [P1]

If the noise continues or you hear loud grinding, stop using the dryer and contact Halvard Home support. [P1]

Stop the programme, switch off and unplug the dryer, and let it cool. Clean and securely refit the fluff filter; if fitted, empty and refit the water tank. Check that no clothing is trapped in the door and close it firmly. Then reconnect the dryer and select the programme again. If the light keeps flashing, stop using the dryer and contact Halvard Home support, explaining which light flashes and when it appears. [P1]

Switch off the washing machine and unplug it. If the water is hot, wait for it to cool completely. Open the lower-front filter flap, put towels and a shallow tray underneath, then loosen the filter slowly so trapped water can drain. Remove debris, rinse the filter, wipe the opening, and refit the filter securely without forcing it. Close the flap, reconnect power, and run a short rinse to check for leaks. [P1]

If it still drains slowly or leaks, stop using the machine and contact Halvard Home support. [P2]

Switch the dryer off at the socket before unplugging it, and use a torch—not a candle—to check the area. If it’s safe to open the door, carefully remove the laundry, which may be hot, and spread it out so heat can escape. [P1]

When the electricity supply is stable, plug the dryer back in, switch it on and check the laundry. Restart a suitable programme if more drying is needed. If you notice a burning smell or visible damage, leave it unplugged and contact Halvard Home support. [P1]

Make sure the dishwasher is switched on and your phone is connected to your home Wi‑Fi. Then move your phone close to the dishwasher, turn on Bluetooth and allow any nearby-device or location permissions the app requests. Avoid guest Wi‑Fi, close and reopen the app, and try adding the dishwasher again. If it still doesn’t appear, switch it off at the mains for 30 seconds, then turn it back on. If the problem continues, contact Halvard Home support and explain what you tried. [P1]

Water underneath your Vale fridge freezer may be from a spill, a blocked defrost drain, or a door that isn’t closing properly. [P1] Water can also collect beneath the appliance because of an incorrectly fitted filter or a damaged connection. [P2]

A rattling or banging noise can be caused by loose objects, an uneven load, or a machine that is not level. [P1]

Pause the programme and wait until the drum stops and the door unlocks—do not force it open. Spread heavy items evenly around the drum, then check for coins, keys, or other loose objects. [P1] If the machine rocks when gently pressed at a corner, switch it off and unplug it before adjusting its feet. [P1] If it was newly installed, check the installation guide to make sure the transit bolts have been removed. [P1]

A factory reset restores the original user settings and removes saved heating schedules and temperature preferences, so note those down first. [P1]

1. Make sure the heat pump is on and not showing a warning. [P1]
2. On the controller, open **Settings**, then select **System** and **Factory reset**. [P1]
3. Choose **Confirm** and leave the power connected while the controller restarts. [P1]
4. When the home screen returns, check the date and time, then re-enter your preferred temperatures and heating schedule. [P1]

If **Factory reset** is unavailable or the controller does not restart, contact Halvard Home support. [P1]
Your old Halvard Home Corra induction hob should be recycled as electrical equipment, not placed in your household rubbish bin. [P1]

To switch on the Brio kettle’s child lock, make sure the kettle isn’t heating, then press and hold the lock button for three seconds; the indicator will light up. [P1]

To switch it off, press and hold the same button for three seconds until the indicator goes out. [P1]

Make sure your fridge freezer is connected to your home Wi‑Fi and has a steady power supply. On the control panel, open **Settings**, select **Software update**, then choose **Check for updates** and follow the on-screen instructions if an update is available. [P1]

Keep the appliance switched on and don’t unplug or restart it during installation. Keep the doors closed as much as possible, and wait for the control panel to confirm the update is complete. If the update fails, check your Wi‑Fi connection before trying again. [P1]

Make sure the kettle has finished boiling and cooled down; do not reset it while it is heating. Place it securely on its base, plug the base into a switched-on wall socket, then press and hold the power button for 10 seconds. Release it when the indicator light flashes twice to confirm the reset is complete. [P1]

If the machine is damp from condensation, wipe the outside with a soft, dry cloth and improve ventilation in the room. Check nearby hoses and connections; recurring puddles may indicate a leak. [P1]

If you notice frost, stop using the machine. Switch it off and unplug it only if your hands, plug and socket are dry. Let the room and machine warm naturally—don’t use boiling water, a hairdryer or a portable heater. [P1] After it has thawed, check for visible leaks. If frost returns or you find damaged hoses, contact Halvard Home support before running another wash. [P1]

Unplug the kettle and let it cool completely. Empty it, open the lid, and gently remove the filter from behind the spout—don’t force it if it feels stuck. Rinse it under warm running water and use a soft brush to loosen deposits. For stubborn buildup, soak it in warm water for 10 minutes, then brush gently and rinse thoroughly. Refit the filter securely before using the kettle. Avoid abrasive cleaners and metal brushes, and never immerse the kettle body, base, or plug in water. [P1]

A factory reset restores the hob’s original settings and clears saved preferences, so note any settings you want to use again. [P1]

1. Remove all cookware, let the cooking zones cool, and make sure the control panel is clean and dry. [P1]
2. Switch the hob off with the power button, but leave its electrical supply connected. [P1]
3. Press and hold the timer and minus buttons together for five seconds. [P1]
4. When you hear a beep, release both buttons, then press the power button once to confirm the reset. [P1]
5. Switch the hob on again and set your preferences. [P1]

If the controls do not respond or the reset does not complete, contact Halvard Home support; do not remove the hob or open its casing. [P1]

Check that the hob has power and your phone is nearby. Turn on Bluetooth and Wi‑Fi, and allow the app access to Bluetooth, nearby devices, and local network if prompted. Then fully close the app, wait 30 seconds, reopen it, and follow the app’s instructions to put the hob into pairing mode before searching again. [P1]

If the hob was connected previously, check whether it appears under another account or home in the app. If you still have trouble, contact Halvard Home support with your phone model and where setup stops. [P1]

To switch the child lock on, press and hold the padlock button for three seconds; the padlock light will come on. To switch it off, press and hold the same button for three seconds, then wait for the light to go out before choosing a programme or changing a setting. [P1]

Use the lowest power setting that keeps food cooking; once water boils, reduce the heat to maintain a gentle simmer. Keep lids on when the recipe allows, use a flat-based induction-compatible pan that matches the zone, heat only the water you need, avoid heating empty pans or excessive preheating, and switch zones off as soon as cooking is finished. If cooking slows too much, increase the power gradually rather than jumping to the highest setting. [P1]
